subject: Emotions
title: Curiosity as Micro-Awe
description: A quick, practical guide to Curiosity as Micro-Awe.

hook.text: A child asks 'why?' about 300 times a day. Each question is a tiny spark of wonder seeking fuel.

buildup.text: Curiosity activates the same reward circuits as surprise. The brain treats an unanswered question as a gap to fill.

discovery.text: George Loewenstein called this the 'information gap theory.' Curiosity is the itch; knowledge is the scratch.

twist.text: Curious students retain 30% more information—not just about the topic they're curious about, but adjacent facts too.

climax.text: Curiosity declines with age not because wonder dies, but because we stop asking questions we can't answer.

punchline.text: Curiosity is awe in miniature, available on demand.

quiz.question: What is the 'information gap theory' of curiosity?
options: Curiosity fills a perceived knowledge gap
